title: Nd:YAG Laser Capsulotomy: A Comprehensive Mastery Guide
summary: Posterior Capsular Opacification (PCO) is the most frequent late complication of cataract surgery. This guide covers the precise clinical application of Nd:YAG laser to restore visual acuity via posterior capsulotomy.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: PCO, or 'after-cataract,' is the opacification of the posterior lens capsule due to the proliferation and migration of residual lens epithelial cells (LECs). Incidence: Up to 20-40% of pseudophakic eyes within 2-5 years. Incidence is higher in younger patients and those with specific comorbidities like Uveitis or Retinitis Pigmentosa.

sections.title: Etiology: The Fibrotic vs. Elschnig Pathway
Clinical Features
content: Reduced visual acuity (gradual onset)
Increased glare and halos
Difficulty with contrast sensitivity
Monocular diplopia
Obscuration of fundus view during exam

sections.title: Indications & Contraindications
content: DO NOT perform if patient is symptomatic (glare/acuity loss) and visual function is not impaired.
Rule out other pathology (e.g., CME, ERM) before blaming PCO.
Caution in high myopes (retinal detachment risk).
Contraindicated in acute ocular inflammation/uveitis.
Corneal edema: Ensure clear view to avoid accidental IOL pitting.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Procedure
content: Step 1: Dilate pupil (Tropicamide 1%).
Step 2: Apply topical anesthesia (Proparacaine) and gel-coupled capsulotomy lens.
Step 3: Set focus. Align YAG laser aim beam on the posterior capsule.
Step 4: Start at 1.0–2.0 mJ energy. Use a circular or 'can-opener' pattern.
Step 5: Ensure IOL offset is set to 'posterior' to avoid IOL pitting.
Step 6: Post-procedure: Check IOP at 1-hour and prescribe NSAID/steroid drops for 3-5 days.

content.explanation: P: Power (start low), I: IOL protection (offset focus), T: Timing (ensure patient symptoms justify procedure), S: Safety (monitor IOP)

sections.title: Complications
content: IOP spikes (up to 30% of cases)
IOL damage (pitting/cracking)
Cystoid Macular Edema (CME)
Retinal Detachment (rare, 0.5-1%)
IOL dislocation

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Advanced IOL materials (hydrophobic acrylic) have significantly reduced PCO rates.
Laser-less prevention: Use of 'Capsule polishing' techniques during phacoemulsification.
Landmark Studies: Focus on the 'Posterior Capsule Opacification' meta-analyses confirming IOL edge design (square-edged) as the gold standard for prevention.
